questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Choose a false statement regarding the properties of sodium hydroxide.
options: the solution of NaOH turns blue litmus red.
NaOH is a white deliquescent solid.
questions.solution:
Sodium hydroxide ($\text{NaOH}$) is a strong base. Basic solutions turn red litmus paper blue. Therefore, the statement that the solution of $\text{NaOH}$ turns blue litmus red is false.

The other statements are true:
$\text{NaOH}$ is highly soluble in water.
It reacts with atmospheric $\text{CO}_2$ to form sodium carbonate ($\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$).
It is a white, deliquescent solid that readily absorbs moisture from the air.

Answer: the solution of NaOH turns blue litmus red.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which element from following forms superoxide with oxygen?
questions.solution:
Alkali metals react with oxygen to form different types of oxides depending on their size.

Lithium forms mainly monoxide (Li_{2}O$).

Sodium forms mainly peroxide (Na_{2}O_{2}$).

Potassium, rubidium, and cesium form mainly superoxides (MO_{2}$) due to the stabilization of the large superoxide ion by large cations.

Magnesium forms mainly monoxide (MgO$).

Therefore, potassium forms a superoxide with oxygen.

Answer: Potassium

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the general formula of halide salts of alkali metals if M is a metal atom ?
questions.solution:
Alkali metals belong to Group 1 of the periodic table and have one valence electron. They lose this electron to form a unipositive ion, $M^{+}$.

Halogens belong to Group 17 and have seven valence electrons. They gain one electron to form a uninegative ion, $X^{-}$.

To form a neutral salt, one $M^{+}$ ion combines with one $X^{-}$ ion.

The general formula of halide salts of alkali metals is $MX$.

Answer: $\text{MX}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from the following metal chlorides does not contain water of crystallisation ?
questions.solution:
Alkali metal chlorides generally do not form hydrates, with the exception of lithium chloride, which is deliquescent and crystallises as a dihydrate, $\text{LiCl} \cdot 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$.

Alkaline earth metal chlorides such as $\text{MgCl}_2$ and $\text{BeCl}_2$ readily form hydrates. $\text{MgCl}_2$ crystallises as a hexahydrate, $\text{MgCl}_2 \cdot 6\text{H}_2\text{O}$, and $\text{BeCl}_2$ crystallises as a tetrahydrate, $\text{BeCl}_2 \cdot 4\text{H}_2\text{O}$.

Caesium chloride ($\text{CsCl}$) is an alkali metal chloride that does not form hydrates and crystallises as an anhydrous salt.

Therefore, $\text{CsCl}$ does not contain water of crystallisation.

Answer: $\text{CsCl}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following compounds is formed when chlorine reacts with dry slake lime $\text{Ca(OH)}_2$ ?
questions.solution:
When chlorine gas is passed over dry slaked lime $\text{Ca(OH)}_2$, bleaching powder is formed.

The chemical reaction is given by:

$\text{Ca(OH)}_2 + \text{Cl}_2 \rightarrow \text{CaOCl}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$

The compound formed is $\text{CaOCl}_2$.

Answer: $\text{CaOCl}_2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the alkali metal having the smallest atomic size from following.
questions.solution:
The alkali metals given in the options belong to Group 1 of the periodic table.

As we move down a group, the number of electron shells increases, which leads to an increase in atomic size.

The order of the given alkali metals from top to bottom in Group 1 is Sodium (Na), Potassium (K), Rubidium (Rb), and Caesium (Cs).

Therefore, the order of their atomic sizes is Na < K < Rb < Cs.

Among the given options, Sodium has the smallest atomic size.

Answer: Sodium

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the elements of alkali metals and alkaline earth metals respectively having highest 1st ionization enthalpy.
questions.solution:
Ionization enthalpy decreases down a group in the periodic table due to an increase in atomic size and shielding effect.

Among alkali metals (Group 1), Lithium ($\text{Li}$) is at the top of the group and has the smallest atomic size, hence it has the highest first ionization enthalpy.

Among alkaline earth metals (Group 2), Beryllium ($\text{Be}$) is at the top of the group and has the smallest atomic size, hence it has the highest first ionization enthalpy.

Therefore, the elements with the highest first ionization enthalpy are $\text{Li}$ and $\text{Be}$ respectively.

Answer: $\text{Li}$ and $\text{Be}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which alkaline earth metal carbonate decomposes most easily?
questions.solution:
The thermal stability of alkaline earth metal carbonates increases down the group from $Be$ to $Ba$.

This is because as the size of the cation increases, its polarizing power decreases. A smaller cation like $Mg^{2+}$ polarizes the large carbonate ion (CO_3^{2-}$) more effectively, weakening the $C-O$ bond and facilitating its decomposition into the metal oxide and $CO_2$.

The order of thermal stability is $MgCO_3 < CaCO_3 < SrCO_3 < BaCO_3$.

Therefore, $MgCO_3$ has the lowest thermal stability among the given options and decomposes most easily.

Answer: \text{MgCO}_3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which colour is developed to the solution when alkaline earth metals are dissolved in liquid ammonia ?
questions.solution:
Alkaline earth metals dissolved in liquid ammonia, analogous to alkali metals, ionize to form metal cations and free electrons, which then solvate with ammonia molecules as ammoniated electrons. These electrons are responsible for the deep blue coloration, high conductivity, and paramagnetic behavior of the solution. At higher concentrations, the solution transitions to a bronze appearance and diamagnetic character due to electron association.

$M(s) + (x+y)NH_3(l) \rightarrow [M(NH_3)_x]^{2+}(am) + 2[e(NH_3)_y]^-(am)$

Ammoniated electrons absorb energy in the visible region, resulting in the transmission of the complementary deep blue color.

The correct option is $\boxed{B}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the element forming peroxide on reaction with oxygen.
questions.solution:
The classification of alkali metals by their oxides is well-established. Lithium forms the normal oxide $Li_2O$, sodium forms the peroxide $Na_2O_2$, and potassium, rubidium, and caesium form superoxides $MO_2$ (where $M = K, Rb, Cs$).

Among the options:
Carbon ($C$) forms $CO$ and $CO_2$, but not peroxides.
Argon ($Ar$) and helium ($He$) are noble gases and inert to oxygen.
Sodium ($Na$) reacts with oxygen according to $2Na(s) + O_2(g) \rightarrow Na_2O_2(s)$, producing sodium peroxide.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is not an alkali metal?
questions.solution:
Alkali metals comprise Group 1 elements: lithium (Li), sodium (Na), potassium (K), rubidium (Rb), caesium (Cs), and francium (Fr).

Beryllium (Be) belongs to Group 2, classifying it as an alkaline earth metal rather than an alkali metal.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following elements form superoxide with air?
questions.solution:
The reaction of alkali metals with oxygen depends significantly on atomic size, as this influences the stability of the resulting oxide compounds.

Lithium forms the oxide $\mathrm{4Li(s) + O_2 (g) \rightarrow 2Li_2 O(s)}$, while sodium yields the peroxide $\mathrm{2Na(s) + O_2 (g) \rightarrow Na_2 O_2 (s)}$.

Larger alkali metals—potassium, rubidium, and cesium—form superoxides such as $\mathrm{K(s) + O_2 (g) \rightarrow KO_2 (s)}$, since their size stabilizes the superoxide ion $\mathrm{O2^{-}}$.

Magnesium, an alkaline earth metal, reacts as $\mathrm{2Mg(s) + O_2 (g) \rightarrow 2MgO(s)}$.

Only potassium forms a superoxide with air.

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{C}}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the product when magnesium burns in air.
questions.solution:
When magnesium burns in air, it undergoes reactions with both oxygen and nitrogen. The primary reactions are:

With oxygen: $2\mathrm{Mg} + \mathrm{O}_2 \rightarrow 2\mathrm{MgO}$

With nitrogen: $3\mathrm{Mg} + \mathrm{N}_2 \rightarrow \mathrm{Mg}_3\mathrm{N}_2$

The products formed are magnesium oxide and magnesium nitride.

Answer: D

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following compound is used for preparation of quicklime?
questions.solution:
Quicklime (calcium oxide, $\text{CaO}$) is industrially prepared through the thermal decomposition of calcium carbonate ($\text{CaCO}_3$), a process termed calcination.

$\text{CaCO}_3(s) \xrightarrow{\text{Heat}} \text{CaO}(s) + \text{CO}_2(g)$

Calcium carbonate (limestone) decomposes at approximately $825^\circ\text{C}$ to yield quicklime and carbon dioxide.

Evaluating the options:
A: Caustic soda ($\text{NaOH}$) is a strong base, irrelevant to quicklime production.
B: Sodium carbonate ($\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$) is washing soda, not used here.
C: Calcium carbonate ($\text{CaCO}_3$) is the correct precursor.
D: Magnesium carbonate ($\text{MgCO}_3$) decomposes to magnesium oxide, not calcium oxide.

questions.solution:
Lithium carbonate decomposes differently from other alkali metal carbonates due to the small size and high polarizing power of the $\mathrm{Li}^+$ ion, which lowers its thermal stability. The decomposition products are lithium oxide and carbon dioxide:

$\mathrm{Li}_2 \mathrm{CO}_3 (s) \xrightarrow{\Delta} \mathrm{Li}_2 \mathrm{O} (s) + \mathrm{CO}_2 (g)$

Among the options, only A provides the correct decomposition products: $\mathrm{Li}_2 \mathrm{O} + \mathrm{CO}_2$.
Option B has an incorrect formula $\mathrm{LiO}$, option C yields an implausible carbide, and option D produces peroxide and carbon monoxide, none of which match.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which halide of magnesium has the& highest ionic character?
questions.solution:
Size of anion is $I^{−} > \text{B}r^{−} > \text{C}l^{−} > F^{−}$. As the size increases, polarisation of an anion is more, hence when covalent character increases ionic character decreases.
Order of ionic character is $\text{M}\text{g}{F}_{2} > \text{M}\text{g}\text{C}{l}_{2} > \text{M}\text{g}\text{B}{r}_{2} > \text{M}\text{g}{I}_{2}$
Hence Magnesium fluoride has the highest ionic character.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is least hydrolysed?
questions.solution: $\mathrm{BeCl}_{2}$ is covalent whereas all other group-II metal halides are electrovalent. Therefore, $\mathrm{BeCl}_{2}$ is least hydrolysed.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When Zn is treated with excess of $\mathrm{NaOH}$, the product obtained is
questions.solution:
When $\mathrm{Zn}$ is reacted with excess of $\mathrm{NaOH}$, sodium zincate is obtained. $\mathrm{Zn}+2 \mathrm{NaOH}+2 \mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Na}_{2}\left[\mathrm{Zn}(\mathrm{OH})_{4}\right]+\mathrm{H}_{2}$ soluble
Or $\mathrm{Zn}+2 \mathrm{NaOH} \longrightarrow \mathrm{Na}_{2} \mathrm{ZnO}_{2}+\mathrm{H}_{2}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Reaction for the formation of $\mathrm{NaCl}$ is
questions.solution: The correct reaction for the formation of $\mathrm{NaCl}$ is $\mathrm{Na}($ s)+$\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{Cl}_{2}($ g) \longrightarrow $\mathrm{NaCl}($ s) (As the compounds are formed from their elements when they are present in their most stable form.)
